notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Connect the professional, the practice and the account.
intro: A proposed lifecycle-data workbench for Heidi: resolve organization relationships before turning product activity into a useful enterprise handoff.
queueIntro: All organizations and professional-use scenarios are fictional. No patient records, clinical notes or personal health information appear in this demo.
workbenchIntro: Check professional affiliation, workspace context and existing ownership. Organization-level product activity can support discovery without making clinical claims.
firstBody: Join professional workspace activity to the right practice and parent organization, preserve conflicting affiliations and give sales or CS a concrete operational question.

fields.label: Usage signal joined to the correct professional workspace
Self-serve and enterprise lifecycle states reconciled

rules.title: Resolve the practice hierarchy
rules.next: Keep the clinician, practice, provider group and parent organization distinct before assigning an account.

rules.title: Review the affiliation evidence
rules.next: Preserve conflicting sources instead of assuming a clinician belongs to only one organization.

rules.title: Validate the product signal
rules.next: Do not attribute a personal or test workspace to an enterprise account without evidence.

rules.title: Reconcile the lifecycle stage
rules.next: A self-serve user can coexist with an enterprise evaluation. Retain both contexts without duplicate outreach.

rules.title: Check the current relationship
rules.next: Preserve the active sales or customer-success owner before proposing an expansion handoff.

rules.title: Make the handoff useful
rules.next: Describe the documentation workflow question without inferring clinical performance or patient outcomes.

ready.title: Ready for a practice-account review
ready.next: The account owner can inspect the affiliation evidence, product context and proposed operational question. This is not a clinical assessment.

experiments.name: Hierarchy-aware account matching
experiments.hypothesis: Practice and parent relationships reduce incorrect enterprise handoffs.
experiments.primary: Correct account handoffs per reviewed workspace
experiments.guardrail: False merges and unsupported affiliation claims
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Operational context in the handoff
experiments.hypothesis: A useful workflow question improves sales and CS acceptance.
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Agree on account and lifecycle definitions
roadmap.body: Map clinician, practice, group and parent entities with Marketing, Sales and CS. Define conflicting-affiliation handling.

roadmap.title: Pilot one product-to-account motion
roadmap.body: Build a versioned identity join and reviewed handoff for an agreed professional-use signal.

roadmap.title: Improve lifecycle measurement
roadmap.body: Connect corrected account data to cohort adoption and commercial outcomes without mixing user and organization denominators.
roadmap.measure: Practice activation, expansion discovery and data quality

metricsTitle: Do not divide organization outcomes by individual users.
metricsIntro: Synthetic identity and lifecycle cohorts use explicit entity levels.
metricsNotes: These are invented operating examples, not Heidi adoption or clinical results.
A user milestone is not automatically a buying signal for the parent organization.
Keep patient data outside GTM research and qualify the business workflow through the appropriate professional contact.
